verses.zh: 那时，非利士人聚集军旅，要与以色列人打仗。亚吉对大卫说：「你当知道，你和跟随你的人都要随我出战。」
verses.en: In those days the Philistines gathered their troops[NOTE:1] for war in order to fight Israel. Achish said to David, “You should fully understand that you and your men must go with me into the battle.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “their camps.”

The translation follows the LXX (εἰς πόλεμον, eis polemon) and a Qumran ms למלחמה (lammilkhamah, “for battle”) rather than the MT’s בַמַּחֲנֶה (bammakhaneh, “in the camp”; cf. NASB). While the MT reading is not impossible here, and although admittedly it is the harder reading, the variant fits the context better. The MT can be explained as a scribal error caused in part by the earlier occurrence of “camp” in this verse.
verses.commentary:
28:1 "in those days" This is another literary marker that the account was written
by an editor or compiler many years after
the events.

▣ "Know assuredly" This is an intensified grammatical construction of an INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
and an IMPERFECT VERB of the same root (BDB 393, KB 390).

▣ "in the camp" The LXX and DSS have "in the battle. The Hebrew is similar. The LXX seems to fit the
context better (NIDOTTE, vol. 2, p. 919, #2; NET, p. 510, #1). So v. 5 should read, "when Saul saw the army."

verses.zh: 大卫对亚吉说：「仆人所能做的事，王必知道。」亚吉对大卫说：「这样，我立你永远作我的护卫长。」
verses.en: David replied to Achish, “That being the case, you will come to know what your servant can do!” Achish said to David, “Then I will make you my bodyguard[NOTE:1] from now on.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the guardian for my head.”
Heb “all the days.”
verses.commentary:
28:2 Achish had been deceived by David. He foolishly even made David his bodyguard (lit. "keeper of my heart").
David will not, cannot fight against his people and his God's people!

verses.zh: 那时撒母耳已经死了，以色列众人为他哀哭，葬他在拉玛，就是在他本城里。扫罗曾在国内不容有交鬼的和行巫术的人。
verses.en: Now Samuel had died, and all Israel had lamented over him and had buried him in Ramah, his hometown.[NOTE:1] In the meantime Saul had removed the mediums[NOTE:2] and magicians[NOTE:3] from the land.
notes: Heb “in Ramah, even in his city.”

The Hebrew term translated “mediums” actually refers to a pit used by a magician to conjure up underworld spirits (see 2 Kgs 21:6). In v. 7 the witch of Endor is called the owner of a ritual pit. See H. Hoffner, “Second Millennium Antecedents to the Hebrew ʾÔḆ,” JBL 86 (1967): 385-401. Here the term refers by metonymy to the owner of such a pit (see H. A. Hoffner, TDOT 1:133).
See Isa 8:19 for another reference to magicians who attempted to conjure up underworld spirits.
verses.commentary:
28:3 Samuel, Saul's prophetic source of divine information, was dead. Saul himself had removed the Canaanite
sources of divine information (i.e., spiritists and mediums, cf. 1 Sam. 15:23).

- spiritists ‒ BDB 396 (lit. "familiar spirit," cf. Lev. 19:31; 20:6,27; Deut. 18:11; Isa. 8:19)

- mediums ‒ BDB 15 (lit. "necromancer," cf. Lev. 19:31; 20:6; Deut. 18:11; 2 Kgs. 23:24; 1 Chr. 10:13; Isa. 8:19;
NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 303-304)

See full note at Deuteronomy 18:11 online.

verses.zh: 非利士人聚集，来到书念安营；扫罗聚集以色列众人在基利波安营。
verses.en: The Philistines assembled; they came and camped at Shunem. Saul mustered all Israel and camped at Gilboa.

verses.zh: 扫罗看见非利士的军旅就惧怕，心中发颤。
verses.en: When Saul saw the camp of the Philistines, he was absolutely terrified.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “he was afraid, and his heart was very terrified.”
verses.commentary:
28:5 As Saul was afraid of Goliath, he is now afraid of the large Philistine army. Unlike David,
who looked to YHWH, Saul focused on the immediate circumstances!

Apparently the Philistines gathered

- their army

- mercenaries (like David and others, Josephus, Antiq. 6.14.1)

verses.zh: 扫罗求问耶和华，耶和华却不藉梦，或乌陵，或先知回答他。
verses.en: So Saul inquired of the Lord, but the Lord did not answer him—not by dreams nor by Urim[NOTE:1] nor by the prophets.
notes: See the note at 1 Sam 14:41.
verses.commentary:
28:6 It is uncertain how Saul "inquired of the Lord." However, he tried but there
was no response from Israel's God (cf. 1 Sam. 14:37). See Contextual Insights, A.

It is interesting to note that the VERB "inquire" (BDB 981, KB 1371, Qal
IMPERFECT with waw) has a positive orientation of requesting information from YHWH
(i.e., Num. 27:21).

But in 1 Sam. 28:7 another VERB occurs (BDB 205, KB 233, Qal
COHORTATIVE; NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 993, 999, esp. #6, p. 995), which has a negative orientation
(i.e., 2 Kgs. 1:2; 1 Chr. 10:14; Ps. 10:4; Isa. 8:19; 19:3; Ezek. 14:7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: URIM AND THUMMIM

verses.zh: 扫罗吩咐臣仆说：「当为我找一个交鬼的妇人，我好去问她。」臣仆说：「在隐・多珥有一个交鬼的妇人。」
verses.en: So Saul instructed his servants, “Find me a woman who is a medium,[NOTE:1] so that I may go to her and inquire of her.” His servants replied to him, “There is a woman who is a medium in Endor.”
notes: Heb “an owner of a ritual pit.” See the note at v. 3.
verses.commentary:
28:7 Saul had banned mediums but he knew there must still be some and his servants knew exactly where one was!

The city of Endor was very close to the Philistine area. Saul must have been desperate to travel there
with a small group.

verses.zh: 于是扫罗改了装，穿上别的衣服，带着两个人，夜里去见那妇人。扫罗说：「求你用交鬼的法术，将我所告诉你的死人，为我招上来。」
verses.en: So Saul disguised himself and put on other clothing and left, accompanied by two of his men. They came to the woman at night and said, “Use your ritual pit to conjure up for me the one I tell you.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Use divination for me with the ritual pit and bring up for me the one whom I say to you.”
verses.commentary:
28:8 Saul disguised himself (it must have been hard because he was noticeably taller than most men) because
he wanted a message from YHWH about the upcoming battle, but he knew if the medium recognized him, then she would
not conjure up (BDB 890, KB 1115, NIDOTTE, vol. 3, pp. 945-948) the dead, on penalty of death.

verses.zh: 妇人对他说：「你知道扫罗从国中剪除交鬼的和行巫术的。你为何陷害我的性命，使我死呢？」
verses.en: But the woman said to him, “Look, you are aware of what Saul has done; he has removed[NOTE:1] the mediums and magicians[NOTE:2] from the land! Why are you trapping me[NOTE:3] so you can put me to death?”
notes: Heb “how he has cut off.”
See the note at v. 3.
Heb “my life.”

verses.zh: 扫罗向妇人指着耶和华起誓说：「我指着永生的耶和华起誓，你必不因这事受刑。」
verses.en: But Saul swore an oath to her by the Lord, “As surely as the Lord lives, you will not incur guilt in this matter!”
verses.commentary: 28:10 It is shocking to me that Saul offers an oath in YHWH's name to a medium!

verses.zh: 妇人说：「我为你招谁上来呢？」回答说：「为我招撒母耳上来。」
verses.en: The woman replied, “Who is it that I should bring up for you?” He said, “Bring up for me Samuel.”
verses.commentary:
28:11 Do mediums have the power to manipulate dead prophets? Is this a true appearance of Samuel? I think
it is but the power did not come from the medium (i.e., she is shocked by the coming of Samuel) but from YHWH. He
wanted to confront His first anointed one last time. YHWH can and does use evil for His purposes (i.e., the cross
of Christ)!

See Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp. 217-218 and Gleason Archer, Encyclopedia of Bible
Difficulties, pp. 180-181.

verses.zh: 妇人看见撒母耳，就大声呼叫，对扫罗说：「你是扫罗，为甚么欺哄我呢？」
verses.en: When the woman saw Samuel, she cried out loudly.[NOTE:1] The woman said to Saul, “Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!”
notes: Heb “in a great voice.”

verses.zh: 王对妇人说：「不要惧怕，你看见了甚么呢？」妇人对扫罗说：「我看见有神从地里上来。」
verses.en: The king said to her, “Don’t be afraid! But what have you seen?” The woman replied to Saul, “I have seen a divine being[NOTE:1] coming up from the ground!”
notes: Heb “gods.” The modifying participle (translated “coming up”) is plural, suggesting that underworld spirits are the referent. But in the following verse Saul understands the plural word to refer to a singular being. The reference is to the spirit of Samuel.
verses.commentary:
28:13

NASB, NRSV, JPSOA
"a divine being"

NKJV, TEV
"a spirit"

NJB
"a ghost"

REB
"a ghostly form"

LXX, Peshitta
"gods"

The MT has elohim (BDB 43). This word is used in several senses. Be sure to read the Special
Topic below.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

▣ "coming up out of the earth" The ancient Israelites buried their dead. Therefore, the dead were in
the ground. This developed into a concept that Sheol was an underground cavern (i.e., Num. 16:30,33; Ps. 55:15;
63:9; 88:1-18; 139:13-16).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?

verses.zh: 扫罗说：「他是怎样的形状？」妇人说：「有一个老人上来，身穿长衣。」扫罗知道是撒母耳，就屈身，脸伏于地下拜。
verses.en: He said to her, “What about his appearance?” She said, “An old man is coming up! He is wrapped in a robe!”Then Saul realized it was Samuel, and he bowed his face toward the ground and kneeled down.
verses.commentary:
28:14 This verse describes Samuel.

- an old man (possible imagery for respected leader, NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 1135, #2)

- wearing a prophetic robe

- the next several verses have Samuel being very direct with Saul, reasserting YHWH's message of judgment

- Saul recognized it was Samuel (v. 1 Sam. 28:20)

verses.zh: 撒母耳对扫罗说：「你为甚么搅扰我，招我上来呢？」扫罗回答说：「我甚窘急；因为非利士人攻击我，　神也离开我，不再藉先知或梦回答我。因此请你上来，好指示我应当怎样行。」
verses.en: Samuel said to Saul, “Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?” Saul replied, “I am terribly troubled! The Philistines are fighting against me and God has turned away from me. He does not answer me anymore—not by the prophets nor by dreams. So I have called on you to tell me what I should do.”
verses.commentary:
28:15 "God has departed from me" Oh my, what a terrible plight! (cf. 1 Sam. 16:14; 18:12; same thing happened
to Samson in Jdgs. 16:20; also note Rom. 1:24,26,28).

The VERB (BDB 693, KB 747, Qal PERFECT) means to "turn away"
or "desert"; the PERFECT stem denotes the permanence of the leaving.

verses.zh: 撒母耳说：「耶和华已经离开你，且与你为敌，你何必问我呢？
verses.en: Samuel said, “Why are you asking me, now that the Lord has turned away from you and has become your enemy?

verses.zh: 耶和华照他藉我说的话，已经从你手里夺去国权，赐与别人，就是大卫。
verses.en: The Lord has done exactly as I prophesied![NOTE:1] The Lord has torn the kingdom from your hand and has given it to your neighbor David!
notes: Heb “just as he said by my hand.”

verses.zh: 因你没有听从耶和华的命令；他恼怒亚玛力人，你没有灭绝他们，所以今日耶和华向你这样行，
verses.en: Since you did not obey the Lord[NOTE:1] and did not carry out his fierce anger against the Amalekites, the Lord has done this thing to you today.
notes: Heb “listen to the voice of the Lord.”
verses.commentary:
28:18-19 Samuel states Saul's disobedience (v. 18) and YHWH's judgment (v. 19). Now Saul knows how he and his
family will perish!

verses.zh: 并且耶和华必将你和以色列人交在非利士人的手里。明日你和你众子必与我在一处了；耶和华必将以色列的军兵交在非利士人手里。」
verses.en: The Lord will hand you and Israel over to the Philistines![NOTE:1] Tomorrow both you and your sons will be with me.[NOTE:2] The Lord will also hand the army[NOTE:3] of Israel over to the Philistines!”
notes: Heb “And the Lord will give also Israel along with you into the hand of the Philistines.”
With the exception of the Lucianic recension, the LXX has here “and tomorrow you and your sons with you will fall.”
Heb “camp.”
verses.commentary:
28:19 "give over Israel along with you" The whole nation suffered because of Saul. This is the eastern concept of
"corporality" (i.e., one person's actions affect the group—Adam, Achan, Jesus).

▣ "you and your sons will be with me" Saul and his sons will be in Sheol as Samuel was.
The Israelites believed in a conscious but joyless afterlife in Sheol until judgment/resurrection day.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?

verses.zh: 扫罗猛然仆倒，挺身在地，因撒母耳的话甚是惧怕；那一昼一夜，没有吃甚么，就毫无气力。
verses.en: Saul quickly fell full length on the ground and was very afraid because of Samuel’s words. He was completely drained of energy,[NOTE:1] having not eaten anything[NOTE:2] all that day and night.
notes: Heb “also there was no strength in him.”
Heb “food.”

verses.zh: 妇人到扫罗面前，见他极其惊恐，对他说：「婢女听从你的话，不顾惜自己的性命，遵从你所吩咐的。
verses.en: When the woman came to Saul and saw how terrified he was, she said to him, “Your servant has done what you asked.[NOTE:1] I took my life into my own hands and did what you told me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “listened to your voice.”
Heb “listened to your words that you spoke to me.”

verses.zh: 现在求你听婢女的话，容我在你面前摆上一点食物，你吃了，可以有气力行路。」
verses.en: Now it’s your turn to listen to your servant! Let me set before you a bit of bread so that you can eat. When you regain your strength, you can go on your way.”
verses.commentary:
28:22-25 This is not the medium being helpful. She wanted Saul to leave her house!

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Would David have actually attacked Saul with the Philistines?

- How did the king inquire of the Lord?

- Did the witch of Endor really call up Samuel from the dead?

verses.zh: 扫罗不肯，说：「我不吃。」但他的仆人和妇人再三劝他，他才听了他们的话，从地上起来，坐在床上。
verses.en: But he refused, saying, “I won’t eat!” Both his servants and the woman urged[NOTE:1] him to eat, so he gave in.[NOTE:2] He got up from the ground and sat down on the bed.
notes: The translation follows many medieval Hebrew mss in reading וַיִּפְצְרוּ (vayyiftseru, “and they pressed”; from the root פָּצַר, patsar) rather than the MT’s וַיִּפְרְצוּ (vayyifretsu, “and they broke forth”; from the root פָּרַץ, parats).
Heb “he listened to their voice.”

verses.zh: 妇人急忙将家里的一只肥牛犊宰了，又拿面抟成无酵饼烤了，
verses.en: Now the woman[NOTE:1] had a well-fed calf[NOTE:2] at her home that she quickly slaughtered. Taking some flour, she kneaded it and baked bread without leaven.
notes: Masoretic mss of the Hebrew Bible mark this word as the half-way point in the book of Samuel, treating 1 and 2 Samuel as a single book. Similar notations are found at the midway point for all of the books of the Hebrew Bible.
Heb “a calf of the stall.”

verses.zh: 摆在扫罗和他仆人面前。他们吃完，当夜就起身走了。
verses.en: She brought it to Saul and his servants, and they ate. Then they arose and left that same night.

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT THE PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Second paragraph

- Etc.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- There were several culturally expected ways for God to give direction.

- dreams, vv. 6,15

- Urim (i.e., ephod of the High Priest), v. 6; see NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 329-330

- prophets, vv. 6,15

- mediums, spiritists, vv. 3,7; see NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 303-304

- Saul had cut himself off from YHWH by his disobedience (v. 18), now YHWH had cut him off.

- Samuel the chief prophet of this period ‒ dead

- High Priest fled to David after Saul had the priests at Nob killed

- Saul himself had banned all spiritists and mediums (v. 3)

- Saul was very afraid (cf. vv. 5,15,20,21), but in the following chapters he still acted on Israel's behalf, knowing
he and his sons would all die in a losing battle.
